name: Sindangan Subanun
confidence_why: Brichoux 1977 states that Sindangan Subanun has no contrastive word stress and that suffixes, unlike enclitics, shift a word's stress, and Arms 1996 independently refers to rules for stress in the Midsalip dialect, so stress is predictable rather than lexical, but no source gives its position and nothing read disagrees.
catalog_citation: Brichoux, Robert. 1977. Spelling Subanun style: a test of a phonemic-cultural orthography. Studies in Philippine Linguistics 1(1): 151-162. Manila: Linguistic Society of the Philippines / Summer Institute of Linguistics. (SIL archive 25624)
catalog_locator: sec. 3.1, p.156 (main statement); sec. 0.27, p.153 (enclitics vs. suffixes); file, pages re-read from the images
catalog_quote: [p.156, sec. 3.1] The question becomes, how shall glottal catch be symbolized? The Pilipino analogs are the grave accent (`) over an unaccented word-final vowel, a circumflex accent (^) over an accented final vowel, and hyphen (-) between a consonant and a vowel. Sindangan Subanun does not have contrastive word stress. In addition, glottal catch does not occur as non-phonemic utterance-initial nor word-initial before otherwise vowel-initial words, as it does in some Philippine dialects. [p.153, sec. 0.27] Certain enclitics are unquestionably part of the phonological word. To write them as separate words has proven to result in halting reading. These enclitics are single syllables which become part of the phonological word, but they do not affect the stress of the word as does a suffix: -u, singular speaker pronoun, subject; -u~-ku, singular speaker pronoun, actor; -a~-ka, singular hearer pronoun, subject; -mu, singular hearer pronoun, actor; -en~-nen, singular referent pronoun, actor; -ta speaker+hearer pronoun, actor; and -i, ligature. Shall they be written as part of the word, separated by a hyphen, or written separately? For example, is "my house" to be written gbalayu, gbalay-u, or gbalay u?
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Sindangan (Central) Subanen is not contrastive (no lexical minimal pairs by stress, hence no accent marks needed in the orthography). Stress is a property of the phonological word whose position is fixed relative to the stem-plus-suffix string: adding a suffix moves it, adding a monosyllabic enclitic pronoun/ligature does not. The source does not say on which syllable (penult or final) the predictable stress falls; Arms 1996 fn.9 likewise refers to 'the rules for stress (not treated in this paper)'. Vowel length (written as double vowels) is a separate, marginally contrastive feature (Brichoux 1970; Arms 1996 fn.21).
new_statements.exceptions: none; only the enclitic/suffix asymmetry (enclitics -u, -ku, -a, -ka, -mu, -en/-nen, -ta, -i are stress-neutral, suffixes are not).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word including suffixes but excluding enclitics; statement made in the context of orthography design (whether accent marks are needed), i.e. about citation/lexical forms. Variety: Sindangan Subanun as tested in Titik and Guigang (Sindangan, Zamboanga del Norte) and Dipurihan and Gluanan (Bayog, Zamboanga del Sur), 1973.
new_statements.identity_note: All quoted material describes 'Sindangan Subanun/Subanen' = Central Subanen [syb], Glottolog cent2089 (Brichoux 1970 fn.2: c. 25,000 speakers in the northern half of Frake's 'Eastern Subanun' area, informants from Barrio Engin and Barrio Titik, Zamboanga del Norte; Brichoux 1977 test communities Titik and Guigang, Sindangan, Zamboanga del Norte, and Dipurihan and Gluanan, Bayog, Zamboanga del Sur). Arms 1996 describes the Midsalip (south-eastern) dialect of the same language. Not to be confused with Siocon/Western Subanon (west2557), Lapuyan/Southern Subanen (lapu1236 / sout2918-type codes), Tuboy/Northern Subanen (nort2885) or Salug/Eastern Subanen (east2694), for which separate descriptions (Hall; Lobel & Hall 2010; Sanicas-Daguman; Bulalang 2025) exist.

sources.note: Sec. 3.1 p.156: 'Sindangan Subanun does not have contrastive word stress.' Sec. 0.27 p.153: monosyllabic enclitics 'become part of the phonological word, but they do not affect the stress of the word as does a suffix' (so stress is predictable and shifts under suffixation); the position of stress is never stated. Cites Brichoux 1972 'Length in Sindangan Subanun' for vowel sequences.

sources.note: Segmental inventory and reflexes for Proto-Subanen and Central Subanen (Tables 10.3-10.5; CSUB retains vowel sequences aa ii uu, ai/au ~ [ee oo]); no statement on Subanen stress. Only a general remark (fn.3 p.287, in the Maranao chapter) that 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress'.

sources.citation: Arms, D. G. 1996. Categories of the Sindangan Subanen verb. In Papers in Austronesian Linguistics 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-84), 1-32. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Only a passing footnote (fn.9, pp.4-5): 'The rules for stress (not treated in this paper) and Rule 2 function as if the underlying form was indeed ew' -- i.e. stress is rule-governed (predictable) but the rules are not given. fn.4 phoneme inventory; fn.21 vowel length has 'a very low functional load'. Midsalip-area dialect.
